paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The line chart displays the cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, plotted against the size of subset S, denoted as |S|, which ranges from 2 to 10 along the linear x-axis with integer tick marks. The y-axis, labeled “Cosine similarity,” is linear and spans from 0.1 to 0.35, with major tick marks at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. Two lines are plotted: the blue dashed line with square markers represents “Weight averaging,” starting at approximately 0.33 at |S|=2 and decreasing to about 0.23 at |S|=10, showing a steep initial drop followed by a gradual leveling off. The green dash-dotted line with circular markers represents “QLoRA,” beginning at approximately 0.29 at |S|=2 and declining to roughly 0.16 at |S|=10, exhibiting a more consistent downward slope throughout the range. Both lines demonstrate a decreasing trend in cosine similarity as |S| increases, with the QLoRA line consistently below the Weight averaging line across all values of |S|.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the average cosine similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models, as a function of the size of subset S, denoted |S|, ranging from 2 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “|S|”, is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The y-axis, labeled “Cosine similarity”, is linearly scaled from 0 to approximately 0.35, with major gridlines and tick labels at 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3. Two methods are compared: “Weight averaging” (blue dashed line with square markers) and “QLoRA” (green dash-dotted line with circular markers). For “Weight averaging”, cosine similarity starts at approximately 0.33 at |S|=2, drops sharply to about 0.28 at |S|=3, then gradually declines to around 0.24 at |S|=10. For “QLoRA”, similarity begins at about 0.29 at |S|=2, decreases to 0.21 at |S|=4, and continues to decline more slowly to approximately 0.17 at |S|=10. Both lines exhibit a downward trend as |S| increases, with “Weight averaging” consistently maintaining higher similarity than “QLoRA” across all subset sizes.
